title: VLAN Tagging
description: Understand 802.1Q tagging and how trunk frames identify their VLAN.
scenario: Understand 802.1Q tagging and how trunk frames identify their VLAN.

concepts.title: Why Tag Frames?
concepts.body: When multiple VLANs cross one physical link, frames need a tag so the receiving switch knows which VLAN they belong to. This is the job of 802.1Q.
concepts.code:
VLAN 10 frame + VLAN 20 frame → one trunk
Trunk frame = original frame + 802.1Q tag

concepts.title: 802.1Q Tag Structure
concepts.body: The 802.1Q tag is 4 bytes inserted after the source MAC: Tag Protocol ID (TPID) + Priority + VLAN ID (VID, 12 bits = 1-4094).
concepts.code:
| Dst MAC | Src MAC | [TPID + VID] | Payload | FCS |
                      ↑ 802.1Q tag

concepts.title: Tagged vs Untagged
concepts.body: Access ports send untagged frames. Trunk ports tag all frames EXCEPT the native VLAN, which is sent untagged.
concepts.code:
Access: Fa0/1 → untagged frame
Trunk: Gi0/1 → tagged + native VLAN untagged

concepts.title: Verifying Tagging
concepts.body: "show interfaces trunk" shows operational mode and encapsulation. "show interfaces switchport" shows switchport admin/operational details.
concepts.code:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port  Mode  Encapsulation  Status  Native vlan
Gi0/1 on    802.1q        trunking  99
